comparison: Perfect agreement on T cell proliferation assays (C72-C74, C221-C223). Both acknowledge the differential responses between DR13 and DR15 mice as interesting observations. OpenEval notes the lack of explanation for DR15 non-responsiveness, while peer reviewers treat this as a notable finding without critique.

Perfect agreement on overall model utility and conclusions (C45, C170-C172, C181, C232-C233, C235-C236). Both acknowledge the model as valuable for MS research despite limitations. OpenEval notes that drug screening claims are speculative, while peer reviewers affirm the model will be used by the MS research community.

Strong agreement on EBV-B cell engraftment correlation (C34, C64, C225-C226). Both treat this as a notable observation. OpenEval emphasizes the correlative rather than causal nature, while peer reviewers acknowledge it as an interesting finding without challenging the interpretation.

Strong agreement on HLA-DRB1-dependent CNS infiltration patterns (C35-C36, C173, C175). Both acknowledge this as a key strength. OpenEval notes limited DR13 MS sample size (n=1), while peer reviewers emphasize the value of using HLA-typed PBMCs without questioning the findings.

Strong agreement on spontaneous CNS lesion development in DR15 MS mice (C37-C38, C99-C109, C122-C123). Both acknowledge CNS pathology as a strength and note patient-specific variation. OpenEval identifies lack of quantitative lesion burden analysis, while peer reviewers highlight variability between donors as valuable.

Disagreement on absence of clinical disease (C85-C86, C124, C180). OpenEval rates this as SUPPORTED (well-documented limitation), while peer reviewers rate as UNSUPPORTED, explicitly identifying 'lack of phenotype' as a significant weakness that undermines the model's disease relevance.

Partial agreement on engraftment and experimental design (C32-C33, C52, C61-C62). Both acknowledge solid engraftment data. OpenEval covers broader methodological claims (C46-C51), while peer reviewers focus on statistical rigor improvements and immune subset characterization including CD4/CD8 ratios (C59-C60, C82).

Partial agreement on peripheral vs CNS CD4/CD8 discordance (C59-C60, C182-C183). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the observation but identifying 'lack of mechanistic data on why CD8 T cells are more enriched' as a weakness.

Agreement on model limitations (C41-C42, C65, C194, C199). Both acknowledge poor monocyte engraftment, lack of demyelination, and absence of clinical disease as key limitations. OpenEval rates these as honestly reported, peer reviewers acknowledge them as inherent model weaknesses.

Agreement on lymphoid structure and antibody response limitations (C84, C207-C208). Both acknowledge absence of organized lymphoid structures and IgG responses. OpenEval covers broader discussion of model limitations and future directions (C199, C201-C209, C234), while peer reviewers focus on these as known B2m-NOG model characteristics.

Minimal overlap on MS pathology comparisons (C184-C185). OpenEval evaluates literature citations comparing model to MS features as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers address CD8 enrichment mechanism as UNCERTAIN, with only tangential connection through MS pathology discussion.

OpenEval evaluated CNS infiltration patterns in DR15 healthy control mice (C89-C98) as SUPPORTED, providing important control comparison. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific control group analysis.

OpenEval evaluated spinal cord pathology in non-immunized DR15 MS mice (C112-C119) as SUPPORTED with statistical evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific anatomical and experimental condition.

OpenEval evaluated EAE immunization effects on CNS infiltration (C39, C127-C139, C168, C174) as SUPPORTED, noting increased CD4+ T cells and altered ratios. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers noted lack of disease phenotype even after immunization.

OpenEval evaluated CNS pathology in immunized DR15 MS mice (C140-C152, C169, C177) as SUPPORTED, documenting large corpus callosum lesions without demyelination. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific immunization condition.

OpenEval evaluated correlation analysis results (C153-C154) as SUPPORTED with statistical significance (p<0.0001), though noting limited biological interpretation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific correlations.

OpenEval evaluated spinal cord pathology in immunized DR15 MS mice (C156-C159) as SUPPORTED, noting equal infiltration between MS and HI mice after immunization. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific comparison.

OpenEval evaluated cytokine production data (C66-C67) as SUPPORTED, demonstrating pro-inflammatory cytokine capability, though functional significance untested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific functional characterization.

OpenEval evaluated lymphoid tissue organization and functional consequences (C80-C84) as SUPPORTED with reasonable inferences about IgG response absence. Peer reviewers acknowledged related limitations (R7) but did not specifically evaluate these organizational claims.

OpenEval evaluated peripheral vs CNS inflammation relationship (C120-C121, C162-C167) as SUPPORTED, noting inverse relationship suggesting CNS inflammation is not simply systemic GVHD consequence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific analysis.

OpenEval evaluated mouse myeloid cell distribution (C70-C71, C197-C198) as SUPPORTED, documenting presence in blood but absence from CNS. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though related to monocyte limitations noted by peer reviewers in R6.

OpenEval evaluated glial cell activation (C93, C110, C133, C155, C178) as SUPPORTED, showing microglia and astrocyte responses at inflammation sites. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this innate immune response characterization.

OpenEval evaluated HLA-DRB1*15 biological context and literature support (C212-C231) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations, noting correlations remain correlative not causal. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific literature contextualization.
